met:468482.summary: This marble head of a mature man with a full, curling beard and long hair falling to the shoulders was carved in the Roman manner and, according to the Metropolitan Museum, later transformed; it may represent Zeus, or Christ, or a Zeus image reworked as Christ. It vividly illustrates how the bearded, majestic image of Christ drew on the long tradition of classical images of the father of the gods.
facts: The Met dates the head to the 3rd or 4th century with a later transformation, and titles it 'Head of Christ or Zeus', leaving the identification open.
The bearded, long-haired type of Christ that became standard from the late 4th century onward owes much to classical images of Zeus and of philosophers.
met:468482.notes: Identification as Christ is uncertain (the museum itself hedges). Kept because the Met lists 'Christ' as a subject, but an editor may prefer to exclude it.
